source: triage of the failing checks of the M-QCD campaign (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_mqcd_*.py; m-qcd/PLAN.md §1.4); curated by MQ-VALIDATE from the campaign records and the scratch experiments named per finding (workspace/tmp/mq-validate/); no tolerance is widened and no failing check is listed away

findings.title: Catani's operator mispredicts the single pole when the Born interferes colour structures joined by different electroweak exchanges (Z and W between the two quark lines of D19; the t- and s-channel W of C07)
findings.checks: rule 4, every point, double-double and binary64, single pole of the leading sector only (D19 QCD^2 QED^6: 9.3e-2 .. 3.4e-1; C07 QCD^4 QED^4: 9.2e-4 .. 2.2e-2); the double poles agree
findings.evidence: rule 1 passes on both rows: our virtual equals MadLoop's per squared split order within 1e-12, poles included, so the virtual is right and the prediction is not (MG5_aMC's own FKS pole check of VBF runs on the same MadLoop virtuals). Minimal reproducer on D19's points, double-double, rule 4 only (workspace/tmp/mq-validate/s2/ew22.py): u d > u d h QCD=0 (Z and W exchange, colour structures delta_13 delta_24 and delta_14 delta_23 interfering) single pole 1.6133954759575e-9 against the predicted 1.4436894729941e-9 (rel 0.105) and 0.335 at point 1, while u c > u c h (Z only, one colour structure) and u c~ > u c~ h agree within 6e-33 .. 3e-31, and the QCD Born u d > u d (the same two colour tensors) within 9e-30. The Python reference path (LoopSlice.evaluate, 34 digits) gives the same virtual and the same prediction as the native executor (s2/catani-D19.log). The double poles agree (the row sums of <T_i.T_k> are fixed by colour conservation); no relabelling of the 4 coloured legs' momenta reproduces the virtual's single pole (all 24 tried, best rel 4.5e-2; s2/perm-D19.log); the deviation is mu-independent (points 0 and 3 share the kinematics, mu_R halved: the same -0.0313 x Born). So the colour-correlated Born of the I operator is wrong when the Born vector's colour components come from different EW exchanges, while the colour-summed Born is right. The single-structure W rows pass (F01, F02, F04, D12, D16, D17, D27, H01).
findings.routed_to: coordinator: owner of the strong I operator's correlated Born (loops/v2/assemble.py _qcd_poles / born_vectors, LoopSlice.dipoles); reproducer u d > u d h QCD=0 against u c > u c h; MQ-VALIDATE re-runs D19 and C07

findings.title: MadLoop's values miss our double-double by up to 3.3e-11 with an own accuracy of 0 .. 1e-16: binary64 noise at C02, D11, A06; a systematic MadLoop error at C01 (massive b) that Recola does not share
findings.checks: rule 1: C01 point 1 finite 3.25e-11 (default tier), C01@params point 1 finite 2.69e-11, C02 point 0 finite 2.1e-12, D11 point 1 single pole 4.27e-12, A06 point 1 single pole 1.18e-12
findings.evidence: Cross-checks run into workspace/tmp/mq-validate/qpref/ (the committed exports read only; MQ-REF's toolkit, references.py run): (a) C01 point 1: MadLoop forced to quadruple precision (--madloop-accuracy 1e-20, status 328) reproduces its binary64 value (finite 5.527401070421307, 3.25e-11 from ours; single and double pole 4.8e-13 from ours, which equal Catani's within 1e-27), while Recola (COLLIER) agrees with our double-double within 1.1e-15 on every coefficient of points 0-3 (finite 5.527401070600913 at point 1); our double-double equals 40 and 60 digits within 1e-31 there (s2/c01ap.log): MadLoop's massive-b result is off, not ours. (b) C02 point 0 and D11 point 1: forced quadruple precision brings MadLoop within 5e-14 and 7e-15 of ours (Recola 5.7e-13, 1.5e-13): binary64 noise of the status-216 runs that MadLoop's estimate does not see. (c) A06 point 1 (a cancelling single pole, 0.12 against a Born of 302): the committed Recola and OpenLoops values are 7.3e-13 and 5.2e-13 from ours, MadLoop 1.18e-12; MLStabThres = 1e-20 cannot force quadruple precision there because MadLoop's binary64 estimate is exactly 0 (status 216 again). Not explained by the input point: double-double at MadLoop's own quadruple-precision point (its ImprovePSPoint=2 projection of the binary64 rounding, supplied_points.madloop_qp_point) gives the same deviations (workspace/tmp/mq-validate/qp/exp.py).
findings.routed_to: MQ-REF: rerun the status-216 points in quadruple precision forced by CTModeRun (the threshold cannot force it where MadLoop's estimate is 0), which resolves C02 and D11; add Recola as the second provider of C01/C01@params (it agrees within 1e-15). User ruling needed for C01: rule 1 (i) cannot hold when the primary is wrong in both precisions while its own accuracy reads 0 (proposal: Recola primary for the massive-b rows, MadLoop recorded as an outlier with this evidence)

findings.title: g g > u u~ u u~ and u u~ > g g g g g: no provider reaches 1e-12 at 2->4/2->5 (MadLoop quadruple precision 1.2e-11 with a 1e-12 IR-relation defect; Recola 5e-11; OpenLoops 2.6e-12)
findings.checks: rule 1: A18 points 0, 2, 3 finite 3.5e-12 .. 1.17e-11 and double pole 1.06e-12; A23 points 0-2 finite and single pole 1.0e-12 .. 3.2e-12
findings.evidence: A18: MadLoop's quadruple-precision values (status 328/329, own accuracy 0) are up to 1.17e-11 (finite) and 1.06e-12 (double pole) from ours; MadLoop's double pole is off its own Born times the universal IR factor by exactly that 1.06e-12 at point 2 (and 3.5e-13 at points 0, 3), while ours equals Catani's within 9e-28 and our Born equals MadLoop's within 2e-15, so MadLoop's loop carries a ~1e-12 systematic error. Third opinions (workspace/tmp/mq-validate/qpref/): OpenLoops (ppjjjj, binary64) 5.5e-13 / 9.8e-13 / 1.2e-12 / 2.6e-12 on the finite part of points 0-3 and <= 1.8e-13 on the poles; Recola (binary64) up to 5.3e-11 with double poles 1.1e-11 off. The deviations do not move when our double-double is evaluated at MadLoop's quadruple-precision input point (qp/exp.py). A23 (MadLoop status 216, own accuracies 1.2e-13 .. 2.3e-12, covering some coefficients; Recola's double poles off the universal factor by up to 4.4e-11): no second provider within 1e-12; a forced quadruple-precision MadLoop 2->5 run was not attempted (estimated hours, HANDOFF §0.1).
findings.routed_to: MQ-REF (OpenLoops ppjjjj as A18's second provider is the closest; a MadLoop quadruple-precision rerun by CTModeRun) and the user: the 1e-12 strict rule 1 at 2->4/2->5 needs a provider accurate to ~1e-13; none of the three is, while our poles meet Catani's within 1e-27

findings.title: G02 point 1: MadLoop's QED^4 Born sector reads 3.58e9 (ours 9.6e-3)
findings.evidence: tests/fixtures/loop/required/mqcd/uux_ttx_mixed.json rows[1].sectors.born QED^4 = 3582980135.555 (and the total Born with it), while the loop sectors of the same point, normalised by MadLoop with its internal Born, agree with ours within 1e-12 and the QED^4 Born of points 0, 2, 3 is 9.5e-3; the runner reads the per-sector Borns from born_matrix.f (madloop_driver.f90 comment), so a runner-side read of that sector is suspect

findings.title: MadLoop's Borns of the references are binary64 evaluations: a soft point and suppressed helicities miss 1e-12
findings.checks: A09@soft point 1 (E_g/sqrt(s) = 1e-5) rule 1 [QCD^6] born 2.73e-11; A08 hel point 0: helicities h---+- and h+++-+ born 9.9e-11 (their Born 3.6e-11 against a summed Born of order 1) and their poles 1.3e-12 .. 8.1e-12, h-+-++ finite 4.5e-12
findings.evidence: A09@soft point 1: the loop coefficients agree within 2.5e-13 (the double pole = universal factor x MadLoop's internal Born), only the reported Born misses; our point equals MadLoop's quadruple-precision point within 4.9e-25, so the input does not explain it; a binary64 Born at a soft point carries the momentum-conservation rounding relative to the soft energy (1e-16 / 1e-5). A08: |ours - MadLoop| = 3.6e-21 for a helicity Born of 3.6e-11, i.e. 2 sqrt(B_h B_max) x 1e-16, the binary64 rounding of the amplitude of a helicity suppressed to 1e-11. The runner takes the per-sector Borns from born_matrix.f (binary64); MadLoop's own quadruple-precision evaluation (status 3xx) holds a quadruple-precision Born
findings.routed_to: MQ-REF (Borns from MadLoop's quadruple-precision evaluation, per sector and per helicity); no change to the 1e-12 rule

findings.title: The binary64 estimate under-reports the error of g g > b b~ h (4FS) up to 100x and of u u~ > u u~ e+ e- 23x
findings.checks: rules 2 and 3, binary64, C05 [QCD^6 QED^2] finite at every point: error 2.34e-10 at E = 2.43e-12 (point 1), 4.8e-12 at 1.96e-13, 1.16e-12 at 3.64e-14, 9.5e-12 at 3.7e-13; D10 point 2 [QCD^6 QED^4] double pole 1.72e-12 at E = 7.55e-14 (also rule 4 binary64)
findings.evidence: double-double passes every rule on both rows (rule 1 within 1e-12 of MadLoop); the binary64 error is real and the one-rotation plus reduction-direction estimate does not bracket it tenfold. An error confined to functions of the invariants (scalar integrals with the small b mass) is invisible to rotations; D10 is the PLAN's '22x case'

findings.title: The native executor fails at the S2 collinear points (theta = 1e-3, 1e-5) in both carriers
findings.checks: eval: points 0-2, double-double CutFailed { DegenerateGram } and binary64 Unstable (families 78 and 80, also on the re-test), no value
findings.evidence: the collinear family of tools/loop_reference/supplied_points.py (the last two final gluons at opening angle theta); MadLoop evaluates them (status 3xx). PLAN §4.1 S2 expects binary64 outside O1 there but double-double and rule 3 to pass
findings.routed_to: MQ-STAB (or the reduction owner): degenerate-Gram handling of the cut reduction at small opening angles

findings.title: 40 digits do not converge to 1e-35 on g g > b b~ (4FS, massive b)
findings.checks: rule 6: AP(40) against AP(60) 1.0e-32 (point 1) and 4.1e-32 (point 2) > 1e-35 on the finite part; AP(40) against double-double passes
findings.evidence: C01 point 1 per virtual component, 40 against 60 digits (workspace/tmp/mq-validate/s2/apcomp.py): the bare loop's finite part 7.6e-33, its poles 1.2e-59; R2, UV, UV external fields, UV local and the Born 1e-59 .. 2e-59. So the arbitrary-precision path of the bare loop's finite part (the scalar integrals with the light massive b, 4FS) loses about 8 of its 40 digits, while binary64 agrees with double-double to 1.4e-15 at the same point (a stable binary64 form, a cancelling or guard-digit-free arbitrary-precision one). AP(40) against double-double passes, double-double against AP(60) agrees to 1e-31. B01 (massive top, 5FS) passes rule 6.
findings.routed_to: coordinator: owner of the arbitrary-precision scalar integrals (bare-loop finite part with small internal masses)
